name: American cheetah
hypothesis: A true cheetah lineage (Acinonyx) lived in Pleistocene North America, represented by Miracinonyx.

events.summary: Placed the North American Pleistocene cat Felis trumani in Acinonyx as the new subgenus Miracinonyx, arguing that the cheetah has a native American ancestry.
Described the Plio-Pleistocene cheetah-like cat Miracinonyx inexpectatus of North America, treating Miracinonyx as a full genus.

publication.title: The Plio-Pleistocene cheetah-like cat Miracinonyx inexpectatus of North America

events.summary: Ancient mitochondrial DNA placed Miracinonyx closest to the puma rather than the African cheetah, so its cheetah-like build is convergent.

publication.title: Evolution of the extinct Sabretooths and the American cheetah-like cat

events.summary: Nuclear paleogenomes confirm Miracinonyx trumani as a puma relative, not a cheetah. Stable isotopes extend its range about 20 degrees of latitude north to the Yukon, where it likely fed on anadromous fish; southern populations were generalist predators.

publication.title: Range and diet diversity in the Pleistocene American “cheetah,” Miracinonyx trumani

name: Brontosaurus
hypothesis: Brontosaurus is a valid genus, distinct from Apatosaurus.

events.summary: Named Brontosaurus excelsus from the Late Jurassic of Wyoming.
Judged Brontosaurus too close to Apatosaurus (Marsh, 1877) to stand as its own genus and sank it as a junior synonym.

publication.title: Structure and relationships of opisthocoelian dinosaurs. Part I: Apatosaurus Marsh

events.summary: A specimen-level phylogenetic analysis of Diplodocidae found Brontosaurus different enough from Apatosaurus to reinstate it as a genus.

publication.title: A specimen-level phylogenetic analysis and taxonomic revision of Diplodocidae (Dinosauria, Sauropoda)

name: Nanotyrannus
hypothesis: Nanotyrannus is a distinct small-bodied tyrannosaur, not a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex.

events.summary: Named the genus Nanotyrannus, a 'pygmy tyrannosaur', for the Hell Creek Formation skull CMNH 7541 first described as Gorgosaurus lancensis.

publication.title: Nanotyrannus, a new genus of pygmy tyrannosaur, from the latest Cretaceous of Montana

events.summary: A study of skull growth across tyrannosaurids interpreted the Nanotyrannus holotype as a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex.
A growth series built from many specimens placed the small Hell Creek tyrannosaurs within the ontogeny of Tyrannosaurus rex.

publication.title: A high-resolution growth series of Tyrannosaurus rex obtained from multiple lines of evidence

events.summary: Argued that Nanotyrannus lancensis is a distinct taxon of small-bodied tyrannosaur rather than a growth stage of T. rex.

publication.title: Taxonomic Status of Nanotyrannus lancensis (Dinosauria: Tyrannosauroidea)—A Distinct Taxon of Small-Bodied Tyrannosaur

events.summary: A nearly mature tyrannosaur skeleton from the 'Dueling Dinosaurs' find in Montana supports Nanotyrannus as a genus separate from Tyrannosaurus; the paper also names a second species, N. lethaeus.

publication.title: Nanotyrannus and Tyrannosaurus coexisted at the close of the Cretaceous

name: “Toroceratops”
hypothesis: Torosaurus is not a separate animal but the fully mature growth stage of Triceratops.

events.summary: Proposed that Torosaurus specimens are fully mature Triceratops, with the frill thinning and opening up late in growth.

publication.title: Torosaurus Marsh, 1891, is Triceratops Marsh, 1889 (Ceratopsidae: Chasmosaurinae): synonymy through ontogeny

events.summary: Argued Torosaurus is a distinct genus: some Torosaurus specimens are not fully mature, and some mature Triceratops show no sign of becoming Torosaurus.

publication.title: Torosaurus Is Not Triceratops: Ontogeny in Chasmosaurine Ceratopsids as a Case Study in Dinosaur Taxonomy

events.summary: Geometric morphometrics of skull shape found Torosaurus falling outside the Triceratops growth trajectory, supporting separate genera.

publication.title: Is Torosaurus Triceratops? Geometric Morphometric Evidence of Late Maastrichtian Ceratopsid Dinosaurs
